title: Work item
description: Coordinator to Generator or Researcher. Exactly one claim. Carries no runtime fields — provider, model, session, budget, and retry state belong to the orchestrator's execution envelope, not here.

target_sha256.description: The frozen target hash. Must match the claim, the artifact, the receipt, and the result.

claim_id.description: Exactly one. A work item covering several claims cannot be failed precisely, so it cannot be escalated precisely either.

dependency_path_to_target.description: How establishing this claim reaches the frozen target. A sub-result with no path back is not progress toward it.

active_obstruction.description: The specific thing blocking direct production, for a Researcher assignment.

blocking_claim.description: The claim that would have to be established to get past this. Naming it is required before choosing a weaker product.

obstruction_sha256.description: Binds the attack to the obstruction dispatched. Researcher is the expensive role and returns once; substituting a softer obstruction mid-run is target drift one level down, with the least oversight in the system.

expected_artifact.description: What must come back, in enough detail that its absence is unambiguous.

verification_tier.description: Which adapter tier this claim requires. Frozen by Explorer before work starts, so a cheap tier cannot be substituted after an expensive one fails.

falsifier.description: What observation would show this approach is not working. Required — an approach with no falsifier cannot report a negative result.

forbidden_drift.description: What must not change. Required and specific — you cannot dispatch a vague worker and expect a sharp answer.

stop_rule.description: When to stop and report rather than continue. Required and specific.

method_family.description: Which family this attempt belongs to, for diversity accounting. Two attempts in one family are one method.

do_not_repeat.description: Routes already ruled out by recorded failures. A dispatch matching one of these is blocked until something actually changed.

mutation_applied.description: Required when re-dispatching a claim that already failed. Names the single axis changed and what was deliberately held constant.

effort_cap.description: Advisory ceiling in domain-defined units. The orchestrator owns real budgets.

expected_information_gain.description: What this probe is expected to tell us, and on what basis. Compared against the observed gain on return; a repeated observation reports no gain.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this packet with payload_sha256 removed: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes. Seals the packet and makes it addressable by later packets — an id alone is a mutable label.

base_revision.description: State revision this was cut against. A long-running role can return against state that moved beneath it; without a base pointer that stale return is silently merged.

attempt.description: Where this sits in the escalation ladder. The ladder is declared mechanical, so the counter needs a typed home — held only in a coordinator's working memory it is a judgement call again.

scheduling.description: How this item is dispatched relative to its siblings. Derived from the parent claim's dependency_mode — the same graph that decides closure also decides concurrency, and reading it only once leaves the parallelism unclaimed.

relation_to_siblings.description: race = an OR group; siblings run concurrently and the first pass cancels the rest. fanout = an AND group; all are required, run them concurrently. solo = no siblings.

sibling_group_id.description: Items sharing this id are siblings under one parent claim.

cancel_on_sibling_success.description: Race semantics. A cancelled sibling is recorded superseded, never FAILED_ATTEMPT — it lost a race, it was not refuted, and marking it failed would poison the do-not-repeat ledger against an approach that may be right elsewhere.

diversity_cell.description: (method family x representation x tier). Every cell gets one candidate before any cell gets a second — correlated fan-out is the same attempt billed several times.

effort_tier.description: Escalates one way, cheapest first. An expensive backend should only see what the cheap pass failed to close.

priority.description: Expected information gain per unit cost. Ordering only — never affects acceptance.

context_pack.description: Advisory context travelling with this item. Capped deliberately: past a small size it crowds out the problem. Must NOT enter the packet's identity hash, or memoization breaks every time memory grows.

self_contained.description: False means this packet needs outside context, which caps concurrency at one — it cannot be fanned out.

obligations.description:
Steps the field's doctrine makes mandatory, carried into the work item so the result has to ANSWER them.

Role evals test the machinery a doctrine points at. They cannot test whether the role read the doctrine: a role that ignored it entirely still passed every check, because everything downstream examines the artifact and nothing examines the process that made it. An obligation is the smallest fix — the doctrine's own mandatory steps, named where the work is issued, and refused when the result does not say what happened.

It cannot verify that a step was done WELL, or done at all. It makes skipping one VISIBLE, which is the difference between a rule and a hope.

required_for.description: statuses that need it; absent means every status above CONJECTURE
